summary.short: 21 CFR § 876.1520 adds a classification for gastrointestinal lesion software detection systems, computer-assisted detection devices used with endoscopy, as Class II (special controls). It sets clinical and non-clinical performance testing, usability, safety, software and labeling requirements. Dated 27 December 2022; no effective date is stated in the text.
summary.long: The FDA rule amends 21 CFR Part 876 (Gastroenterology-Urology Devices) by adding § 876.1520 to subpart B. It identifies a gastrointestinal lesion software detection system as a computer-assisted detection device used with endoscopy to detect abnormal gastrointestinal lesions, which may include hardware that interfaces with an endoscope. The device is classified as Class II (special controls). The special controls require clinical performance testing covering detection of lesions and evaluation of adverse events; non-clinical performance testing, including standalone algorithm performance, pixel-level image-quality degradation, marker-annotation video delay and real-time endoscopic video delay; usability assessment; electromagnetic compatibility, electrical, mechanical and thermal safety testing for hardware; and software verification, validation and hazard analysis with a detailed technical software description. Labeling must include instructions for use, warnings against overreliance and against diagnostic use, and summaries of clinical and standalone performance testing. The text cites 21 U.S.C. provisions as its authority. It contains no penalty or enforcement provisions and no numeric thresholds.](truncated)
